title: Why You Should Be Strict On Dress Codes
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin takes on the argument that student dress is just self-expression that shouldn't be policed, and counters that when viewed through the lens of learning and safety, a loosely enforced dress code is a mistake. He lays out seven ways permissive dress undermines a classroom: it fails to transfer high expectations to attitude and work; it distracts from the mission of learning; it pressures students under existing social-media conformity pressure; it discourages enthusiasm by normalizing an 'I don't care' posture; it neglects the lesson that real-world settings have standards; it separates students along social lines of cool versus uncool; and it disrespects boundaries, since permissiveness in one area of classroom management bleeds into others. He frames dress standards as one of many small details — alongside room environment, cleanliness, and procedures — that together form the foundation of an effective classroom, promising a future article with specific SCM dress code recommendations.
points: A loosely enforced dress code is framed not as a matter of taste but as a detractor from learning and safety.
Casual, careless dress trains a casual, careless attitude that transfers to schoolwork and behavior generally.
Removing dress-code guardrails increases pressure to conform to social trends rather than reducing pressure.
Permissiveness in one area of classroom management (dress) tends to bleed into permissiveness in other areas, like respect.
Dress standards join room environment, cleanliness, and clear procedures as small details that build an effective classroom foundation.
quotes: Who cares if students wear their pants below their waist or show more skin than you’re comfortable with? As long as it doesn’t interfere with your teaching, what’s the big deal?
Small details of high expectations—like asking students to keep their work areas impeccable—transfer excellence to everything you do as a class.
Some of the current clothing trends among young people aren’t close to appropriate for school or their age. They clearly distract from the mission of learning.
Removing dress-code guardrails creates anxiety in many students. It pressures them to conform and be part of the cool group. It allows for less freedom, not more.
In fact, permissiveness in any one area of classroom management leads to deterioration in the rest. High standards must be across the board.
Your pursuit of excellence is contingent upon your demand of every detail. It’s not the big things. It’s the little things that communicate your expectations.
